answer: In an agent marketplace selling terrace plans, velvet, and gale forecasts, every seller must lock a $100 bond for 30 days to receive one daily auction bid. Splitting into a thousand identities therefore requires $100,000 locked at once; creating names alone buys no extra bids. The fixed lock prevents recycling one bond across accounts, so a sybil swarm pays a capital and liquidity cost proportional to its auction access.
